messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Documentation Work
parts:
I've been considering putting a little bit of time in on ggplot2's documentation (within R), but before I invested much time I wanted to check what other projects/work was going on. (The proximate instigation for this is the lack of the list of valid aesthetics for each geom, like what's on Hadley's website. geom_point has them, but I think that's it.)

I seem to recall Hadley mentioning that he was working on a new version of his web docs, and I sort of got the impression that the intention was for those to serve as the "primary" documentation. 

So I'm curious what the state of things is right now, so I'm not duplicating efforts, or wasting my time on something...

- Joran

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Documentation Work
parts:
I think that would be really helpful. As far as I know, not much is currently being done. You can go ahead and just submit pull requests.

The new web docs are auto-generated from the R documentation, so it would be best to make changes to the roxygen help entries (above each function).

-Winston
